key_insight: A local LLM layered with other detectors offered two PHI-detection trade-offs: higher recall with lower precision, or similar recall with higher precision than Stanford/Penn on nursing notes.
clinical_relevance: The toolkit could support clinical-text de-identification without sending text off-site, but residual missed PHI still requires privacy safeguards.
method: Combined rule-based detectors, clinical NER and a locally hosted 26B mixture-of-experts LLM.
Evaluated recall-first and precision-first configurations fixed on tuning splits; processing fails closed on detector errors.
Compared with five tools using paired patient-level bootstrap intervals.
evidence_signal: Reporting sets included nursing notes (889 PHI spans) and semi-synthetic discharge summaries (29,023 spans); recall-first detection reached 98.9% and 95.3%, respectively, and all four prespecified comparisons held.
watch_item: Discharge-summary gains over Stanford/Penn were almost entirely on generated untyped names, limiting conclusions about performance on real-world clinical text.
paper_title: A local language model layered with rule-based and neural detectors for clinical text de-identification: an open-source toolkit and evaluation
